Brassica growth under fertiliser and mite infestation

Margarida Antunes

2023-06-06

Data and packages

library(tidyverse)
library(lme4)
library(car)
library(emmeans)
data <- read.csv("data/data2.csv", sep = ";", na.strings = "NA") %>%
  mutate(Mite_ID = factor(Mite_ID),
         # growth between measurements
         H1_H2 = P_height_2 - P_height,
         H2_H3 = P_height_3 - P_height_2,
         L1_L2 = P_leaves_2 - P_leaves,
         L2_L3 = P_leaves_3 - P_leaves_2,
         P1_P2 = P_pistil_VIZ_2 - P_pistil_VIZ,
         P2_P3 = P_pistil_VIZ_3 - P_pistil_VIZ_2)

Data preparation

Plants were measured at three time points (weeks 4, 6 and 7). The data are reshaped from one row per plant to one row per plant per time point.

# Measurements from one time point (n = 1, 2 or 3)
timepoint <- function(n, week) {
  sfx <- if (n == 1) "" else paste0("_", n)
  data.frame(
    ID = data$ID, Block = data$Block, Pot = data$Pot, Plant = data$Plant,
    Nutrient = data$Nutrient, Mite_ID = data$Mite_ID, Replica = data$Replica,
    Ecosystem = data$Ecosystem,
    Date   = data[[paste0("Date_", n)]],
    Leaves = data[[paste0("P_leaves", sfx)]],
    Height = data[[paste0("P_height", sfx)]],
    Pistil = data[[paste0("P_pistil_VIZ", sfx)]],
    Mites  = data[[paste0("Mite_N", sfx)]],
    Week   = week
  )
}

d1 <- timepoint(1, "W4")
d2 <- timepoint(2, "W6")
d3 <- timepoint(3, "W7")

# All time points (used for descriptive plots)
dt <- bind_rows(d1, d2, d3) %>% mutate(Week = factor(Week))

# Weeks 6 and 7, with week-4 values as the initial (baseline) measurement
dt2 <- bind_rows(d2, d3)
baseline <- d1 %>% select(ID, InLeaves = Leaves, InHeight = Height)
dt3 <- inner_join(dt2, baseline, by = "ID")

# Only plants that received mites
dt_mites <- dt3 %>% filter(Mite_ID != "No")

# Total mites per pot, for plants with mites
count_block <- data %>%
  filter(Mite_ID != "No") %>%
  group_by(Block, Mite_ID, Nutrient, Ecosystem, Pot) %>%
  summarise(Mite_total2 = sum(Mite_N_2),
            Mite_total3 = sum(Mite_N_3),
            .groups = "drop")
# Histogram + Shapiro-Wilk test
check_normality <- function(x, title, xlab) {
  hist(x, main = title, xlab = xlab)
  shapiro.test(x)
}

# Estimated marginal means with 95% CI, one panel per level of `panel`
mite_colours <- c("#00BFC4", "#F8766D", "#7CAE00", "#C77CFF", "#FFC300")

plot_emmeans <- function(means, x, panel, ylab, dodge = -0.2) {
  ggplot(means, aes(x = .data[[x]], y = emmean, group = .data[[panel]])) +
    facet_wrap(reformulate(panel), ncol = 4) +
    geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = lower.CL, ymax = upper.CL), colour = "black",
                  width = 0, linewidth = 0.75, alpha = 0.66,
                  position = position_dodge(dodge)) +
    geom_line() +
    geom_point(aes(fill = Mite_ID), shape = 21, size = 2.5, stroke = 1,
               position = position_dodge(dodge)) +
    ylab(ylab) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = mite_colours) +
    theme_bw() + theme(aspect.ratio = 1)
}

Models

All models are linear mixed-effects models with week nested within ecosystem as random effects, tested with Type III F-tests.

Height

Model 1: Height ~ Initial height + Nutrient × Mite origin + (1 | Week/Ecosystem)

model1 <- lmer(Height ~ InHeight + Nutrient * Mite_ID + (1 | Week/Ecosystem), data = dt3)
Anova(model1, type = "III", test.statistic = "F")
## Analysis of Deviance Table (Type III Wald F tests with Kenward-Roger df)
## 
## Response: Height
##                         F Df Df.res  Pr(>F)    
## (Intercept)      453.0458  1  29.49 < 2e-16 ***
## InHeight         332.7370  1 704.79 < 2e-16 ***
## Nutrient           6.3389  1  53.39 0.01485 *  
## Mite_ID            1.3399  2  53.34 0.27053    
## Nutrient:Mite_ID   0.2179  2  52.94 0.80496    
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
summary(model1)
## Linear mixed model fit by REML ['lmerMod']
## Formula: Height ~ InHeight + Nutrient * Mite_ID + (1 | Week/Ecosystem)
##    Data: dt3
## 
## REML criterion at convergence: 7714.4
## 
## Scaled residuals: 
##     Min      1Q  Median      3Q     Max 
## -4.7371 -0.6685 -0.0143  0.7272  2.9660 
## 
## Random effects:
##  Groups         Name        Variance Std.Dev.
##  Ecosystem:Week (Intercept)  103.261 10.162  
##  Week           (Intercept)    6.679  2.584  
##  Residual                   2675.370 51.724  
## Number of obs: 720, groups:  Ecosystem:Week, 60; Week, 2
## 
## Fixed effects:
##                        Estimate Std. Error t value
## (Intercept)           154.25670    7.23883  21.310
## InHeight                0.71678    0.03915  18.309
## NutrientF              20.39893    8.10194   2.518
## Mite_IDM(t)           -11.92519    8.09429  -1.473
## Mite_IDNo              -1.00894    8.12172  -0.124
## NutrientF:Mite_IDM(t)  -3.79539   11.42545  -0.332
## NutrientF:Mite_IDNo    -7.55068   11.43893  -0.660
## 
## Correlation of Fixed Effects:
##             (Intr) InHght NtrntF M_IDM( Mt_IDN NF:M_IDM
## InHeight    -0.560                                     
## NutrientF   -0.512 -0.078                              
## Mite_IDM(t) -0.520 -0.065  0.502                       
## Mite_IDNo   -0.496 -0.105  0.504  0.503                
## NtF:M_IDM()  0.383  0.021 -0.706 -0.707 -0.354         
## NtrnF:M_IDN  0.364  0.053 -0.708 -0.356 -0.708  0.500
means_height <- as.data.frame(emmeans(model1, specs = pairwise ~ Nutrient * Mite_ID)$emmeans)
means_height
##  Nutrient Mite_ID   emmean       SE    df lower.CL upper.CL
##  C        M(b)    240.0876 6.030304 14.52 227.1972 252.9781
##  F        M(b)    260.4866 5.996702 14.21 247.6425 273.3306
##  C        M(t)    228.1625 5.997684 14.22 215.3171 241.0078
##  F        M(t)    244.7660 6.003476 14.27 231.9127 257.6193
##  C        No      239.0787 6.000603 14.24 226.2293 251.9281
##  F        No      251.9270 6.001658 14.25 239.0761 264.7778
## 
## Degrees-of-freedom method: kenward-roger 
## Confidence level used: 0.95

Results

  • Initial height: P < 2e-16 (estimate = 0.717)
  • Nutrient: P = 0.015 (estimate = 20.4)

Conclusion. Plants that started taller stayed taller: each extra mm of initial height predicted about 0.7 mm more height later. Fertiliser increased height by about 20 mm compared with control plants.

From the plots, plants with mites from tomato were the smallest and plants with mites from bean the tallest. Mites from tomato may be more costly to the plant.

plot_emmeans(means_height, x = "Nutrient", panel = "Mite_ID",
             ylab = "Height in mm (estimated marginal means)")

plot_emmeans(means_height, x = "Mite_ID", panel = "Nutrient",
             ylab = "Height in mm (estimated marginal means)")

Leaves

Model 2: Leaves ~ Initial leaves + Nutrient × Mite origin + (1 | Week/Ecosystem)

model2 <- lmer(Leaves ~ InLeaves + Nutrient * Mite_ID + (1 | Week/Ecosystem), data = dt3)
Anova(model2, type = "III", test.statistic = "F")
## Analysis of Deviance Table (Type III Wald F tests with Kenward-Roger df)
## 
## Response: Leaves
##                        F Df Df.res    Pr(>F)    
## (Intercept)      23.3403  1   4.39 0.0066670 ** 
## InLeaves         16.1674  1 711.98 6.417e-05 ***
## Nutrient         12.5519  1  52.86 0.0008366 ***
## Mite_ID           2.5536  2  53.36 0.0872768 .  
## Nutrient:Mite_ID  5.0930  2  52.97 0.0094827 ** 
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
summary(model2)
## Linear mixed model fit by REML ['lmerMod']
## Formula: Leaves ~ InLeaves + Nutrient * Mite_ID + (1 | Week/Ecosystem)
##    Data: dt3
## 
## REML criterion at convergence: 3063
## 
## Scaled residuals: 
##     Min      1Q  Median      3Q     Max 
## -2.3265 -0.6394 -0.1069  0.4016  5.2442 
## 
## Random effects:
##  Groups         Name        Variance Std.Dev.
##  Ecosystem:Week (Intercept) 0.2068   0.4547  
##  Week           (Intercept) 0.2024   0.4499  
##  Residual                   3.9257   1.9813  
## Number of obs: 720, groups:  Ecosystem:Week, 60; Week, 2
## 
## Fixed effects:
##                       Estimate Std. Error t value
## (Intercept)            2.32535    0.48088   4.836
## InLeaves               0.26685    0.06618   4.032
## NutrientF              1.15777    0.32679   3.543
## Mite_IDM(t)            0.28385    0.32710   0.868
## Mite_IDNo             -0.45009    0.32845  -1.370
## NutrientF:Mite_IDM(t) -0.39939    0.46252  -0.864
## NutrientF:Mite_IDNo    1.03005    0.46257   2.227
## 
## Correlation of Fixed Effects:
##             (Intr) InLevs NtrntF M_IDM( Mt_IDN NF:M_IDM
## InLeaves    -0.576                                     
## NutrientF   -0.336 -0.007                              
## Mite_IDM(t) -0.314 -0.044  0.500                       
## Mite_IDNo   -0.280 -0.101  0.498  0.501                
## NtF:M_IDM()  0.217  0.041 -0.707 -0.708 -0.356         
## NtrnF:M_IDN  0.215  0.043 -0.707 -0.355 -0.707  0.501
means_leaves <- as.data.frame(emmeans(model2, specs = pairwise ~ Nutrient * Mite_ID)$emmeans)
means_leaves
##  Nutrient Mite_ID   emmean        SE   df lower.CL upper.CL
##  C        M(b)    3.483918 0.3933202 1.97 1.765232 5.202604
##  F        M(b)    4.641689 0.3932674 1.97 2.922335 6.361044
##  C        M(t)    3.767767 0.3931989 1.97 2.047546 5.487988
##  F        M(t)    4.526146 0.3933856 1.97 2.808284 6.244008
##  C        No      3.033827 0.3938332 1.98 1.321572 4.746081
##  F        No      5.221653 0.3932114 1.97 3.501590 6.941716
## 
## Degrees-of-freedom method: kenward-roger 
## Confidence level used: 0.95

Results

  • Initial leaves: P = 6.4e-05 (estimate = 0.27)
  • Nutrient: P = 0.00084 (estimate = 1.16)
  • Nutrient × Mite origin: P = 0.0095 (df = 2)
    • Fertiliser × tomato mites: estimate = -0.40
    • Fertiliser × no mites: estimate = 1.03

Conclusion. Plants with more leaves at the start kept having more leaves (about 0.3 more per initial leaf). Fertilised plants had about 1.2 more leaves.

The fertiliser effect depended on mite origin: compared with plants carrying bean mites, it was about 0.4 leaves smaller with tomato mites and about 1 leaf larger without mites. The largest fertiliser effect was in plants without mites, which suggests that mites may counteract the benefit of fertiliser.

plot_emmeans(means_leaves, x = "Nutrient", panel = "Mite_ID",
             ylab = "Total leaves (estimated marginal means)")

plot_emmeans(means_leaves, x = "Mite_ID", panel = "Nutrient",
             ylab = "Total leaves (estimated marginal means)")

Pistils

Model 3: Pistils ~ Nutrient × Mite origin + (1 | Week/Ecosystem)

model3 <- lmer(Pistil ~ Nutrient * Mite_ID + (1 | Week/Ecosystem), data = dt3,
               control = lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa"))
Anova(model3, type = "III", test.statistic = "F")
## Analysis of Deviance Table (Type III Wald F tests with Kenward-Roger df)
## 
## Response: Pistil
##                         F Df Df.res    Pr(>F)    
## (Intercept)      371.5135  1 24.462 2.672e-16 ***
## Nutrient           9.0193  1 53.000  0.004071 ** 
## Mite_ID            0.2436  2 53.000  0.784675    
## Nutrient:Mite_ID   0.4076  2 53.000  0.667313    
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
summary(model3)
## Linear mixed model fit by REML ['lmerMod']
## Formula: Pistil ~ Nutrient * Mite_ID + (1 | Week/Ecosystem)
##    Data: dt3
## Control: lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa")
## 
## REML criterion at convergence: 4687.8
## 
## Scaled residuals: 
##     Min      1Q  Median      3Q     Max 
## -2.0701 -0.6549 -0.1861  0.4284  6.6172 
## 
## Random effects:
##  Groups         Name        Variance  Std.Dev. 
##  Ecosystem:Week (Intercept) 8.452e-01 9.193e-01
##  Week           (Intercept) 1.995e-13 4.466e-07
##  Residual                   3.926e+01 6.265e+00
## Number of obs: 720, groups:  Ecosystem:Week, 60; Week, 2
## 
## Fixed effects:
##                       Estimate Std. Error t value
## (Intercept)            12.3667     0.6416  19.275
## NutrientF               2.7250     0.9074   3.003
## Mite_IDM(t)             0.6167     0.9074   0.680
## Mite_IDNo               0.4333     0.9074   0.478
## NutrientF:Mite_IDM(t)  -1.1583     1.2832  -0.903
## NutrientF:Mite_IDNo    -0.5583     1.2832  -0.435
## 
## Correlation of Fixed Effects:
##             (Intr) NtrntF M_IDM( Mt_IDN NF:M_IDM
## NutrientF   -0.707                              
## Mite_IDM(t) -0.707  0.500                       
## Mite_IDNo   -0.707  0.500  0.500                
## NtF:M_IDM()  0.500 -0.707 -0.707 -0.354

## optimizer (bobyqa) convergence code: 0 (OK)
## boundary (singular) fit: see help('isSingular')
means_pistil <- as.data.frame(emmeans(model3, specs = pairwise ~ Nutrient * Mite_ID)$emmeans)
means_pistil
##  Nutrient Mite_ID   emmean        SE    df lower.CL upper.CL
##  C        M(b)    12.36667 0.6416015 24.46 11.04379 13.68955
##  F        M(b)    15.09167 0.6416015 24.46 13.76879 16.41455
##  C        M(t)    12.98333 0.6416015 24.46 11.66045 14.30621
##  F        M(t)    14.55000 0.6416015 24.46 13.22712 15.87288
##  C        No      12.80000 0.6416015 24.46 11.47712 14.12288
##  F        No      14.96667 0.6416015 24.46 13.64379 16.28955
## 
## Degrees-of-freedom method: kenward-roger 
## Confidence level used: 0.95

Results

  • Nutrient: P = 0.004 (estimate = 2.73)

Conclusion. Fertilised plants had about 3 more pistils than control plants, which suggests a higher potential reproductive output.

plot_emmeans(means_pistil, x = "Nutrient", panel = "Mite_ID",

Mites

Model 4: Mites ~ Nutrient × Mite origin + (1 | Week/Ecosystem), plants with mites only

Anova(model4, type = "III", test.statistic = "F")
## Analysis of Deviance Table (Type III Wald F tests with Kenward-Roger df)

summary(model4)

##  Nutrient Mite_ID   emmean        SE   df lower.CL upper.CL

Conclusion. No effect was significant. Mite origin was close to significance, with fewer mites from tomato than from bean.

Descriptive plots

boxplot_by_week <- function(df, y, fill = NULL) {
  mapping <- if (is.null(fill)) aes(x = Nutrient, y = .data[[y]])
             else aes(x = Nutrient, y = .data[[y]], fill = .data[[fill]])
  ggplot(df, mapping) +
    geom_boxplot() +
    facet_grid(cols = vars(Week))
}

boxplot_by_week(dt,  "Height")

boxplot_by_week(dt,  "Height", fill = "Mite_ID")

boxplot_by_week(dt,  "Leaves")

boxplot_by_week(dt,  "Leaves", fill = "Mite_ID")

boxplot_by_week(dt2, "Pistil")

boxplot_by_week(dt2, "Pistil", fill = "Mite_ID")

boxplot_by_week(dt2, "Mites")

boxplot_by_week(dt2, "Mites",  fill = "Mite_ID")

ggplot(count_block, aes(x = Nutrient, y = Mite_total2)) +
  geom_boxplot() + facet_grid(cols = vars(Mite_ID)) +
  ylab("Total mites per pot (measurement 2)")

ggplot(count_block, aes(x = Nutrient, y = Mite_total3)) +
  geom_boxplot() + facet_grid(cols = vars(Mite_ID)) +
  ylab("Total mites per pot (measurement 3)")
